item.title: That gap of more than $420 million is public money, and it should be accounted for line by line
item.description: https://www.kare11.com/article/news/investigations/kare-11-investigates-private-prison-was-on-sale-for-75-million-ice-paid-495-million/89-4b28b6c7-8823-42b3-9f70-95a78f714e18 APPLETON, Minn. — New records obtained by KARE 11 show the company that owned a vacant private prison in Appleton, Minnesota offered to sell it to the state in 2025 for $75 million. One year later, the Trump administration agreed to use taxpayer funds to buy the same abandoned prison from CoreCivic, Inc., for $495.6 million. The price difference, $420 million, is more than taxpayers are estimated to have lost in Minnesota’s much-publicized Feeding Our Future fraud scandal. A Shuttered Prison In the tiny western Minnesota town of Appleton, population less than 1,400, sits the site of what’s been described as the most expensive property purchase in Minnesota history: a 34-year-old vacant prison, shuttered for 16 years. In August, the federal Department of Homeland Security purchased the Prairie Correctional Facility from CoreCivic, Inc, to use it as an ICE detention center.
